tldr: Under a designed minimum-variance baseline, stationary latent confounding and measurement error cancel from covariance differences.  No common all-target reference is needed: the aggregate carrier \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) has rank \(r\) and contains every shift range whenever shifts are nonnegative and every target changes in at least one environment.  A size-\(r\) label set is compatible exactly when some ordering passes the aggregate principal-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) certificate, and every certificate has an acyclic Gaussian realization at any positive-definite baseline with strictly positive structural and measurement noises.  Subset-memoized pivots compute the complete family, while feasible-point augmentation gives always-nonempty honest family regions.  Information distance separates consistency from bounded-information impossibility, but local optimal certification is indexed by the full tangent-cone geometry rather than by distance alone.
gap: Unknown-target methods with latent confounding return candidate supersets, whereas covariance-difference methods recover a global mixing matrix only under profile separation.  Bacchiocchi et al. first give sign/permutation, distinct-eigenvalue, and eigen-decomposition results and later study multiplicity through restricted HSVAR rotation sets, not the complete family of observed causal target labels.
fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if labeled-fiber theorem, an arbitrary-baseline positive-noise converse, a precise boundary result for signed shifts and split references, a complete subset recursion, and honest classification inference whose nonclosed-model selector and information boundary remain valid at covariance-profile collisions.
